proposed_relationship: Mechanical cleavage of hexagonal boron nitride can produce strictly two-dimensional crystals of h-BN, which, despite being thermodynamically unstable, can be stabilized by rolling them into boron nitride nanotubes.
mechanism: The mechanism involves the application of mechanical cleavage to layered hexagonal boron nitride, exploiting the weak van der Waals forces holding the layers together to thin the material down to a single layer. This single layer, though unstable on its own due to thermodynamic principles, can then be rolled into a nanotube structure, which stabilizes it through the formation of a curved, three-dimensional structure from a two-dimensional sheet. This process leverages the known properties of both hexagonal boron nitride and boron nitride nanotubes to achieve a stable, two-dimensional crystal in a nanotube form.
constraint_released: The constraint of thermodynamic instability of strictly two-dimensional crystals at finite temperature is released by stabilizing them through the formation of nanotubes.
predicted_quantitative_outcome: 10^-9 meters (the approximate diameter of a boron nitride nanotube that could be produced through this method)
